issue_title: Redirected requests mishandle method, body, and headers for some status codes
issue_body: Following an HTTP redirect does not always reshape the request the way the redirect status requires. For some redirect responses a POST is downgraded and its body is discarded when the method and body should have been carried through unchanged. Separately, a redirect that is supposed to be re-issued as a plain GET still forwards request headers that describe the original payload, so the redirected request carries header information that no longer applies. Other redirect responses behave correctly. The public method/body and request-header outcome should match the documented behavior for each redirect status.

Separately, a redirect that is supposed to be re-issued as a plain GET still forwards request headers that describe the original payload, so the redirected request carries header information that no longer applies. Other redirect responses behave correctly. The public method/body and request-header outcome should match the documented behavior for each redirect status.
expected_behavior: 301 and 302 redirects of a POST become GET with no body.
303 redirects become GET with no body and drop payload-describing request headers.
307 and 308 redirects preserve the original method and body.
307 and 308 redirects preserve payload-describing request headers.
A redirected GET stays a GET.
Behavior is consistent across all redirect status codes, not just the most common ones.
